intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage report

Invocation start: 2026-11-16T03:14:54Z (host clock, `date -u`; epoch ms 1794798894000).
Story: SEED-380#speed-up-the-slowest-dashboard-frontend-unit-tests (.planning/seeds/SEED-380-speed-up-the-slowest-dashboard-frontend-unit-tests.md); plan .planning/slice-plans/653-speed-up-the-slowest-dashboard-frontend-unit-tests/PLAN.md, slice 6 / G6.
Revision: 7bb49ed863be027a9cdb054c749ca4f95e714ab6 (claude/speed-up-the-slowest-dashboard-frontend-unit-tes).

Promise: "same behavioral protection". The story's example is: "Given two cases in the group that prove the same rule, one is removed or merged only after the surviving case is shown to catch the same failure." Selected rule: after a Done project refresh and a Project Intent visit, returning to the Done story restores the reading pane's scroll place (reading place) on the selected historical Purpose file. Execution had break-checked only selection and Proof-tab keeping in the merged survivor. The reading-place assertion moved over from the merged -reading case without its own break.

Fault (caller suggestion validated and used): in dashboard/src/pageIntentReading.tsx, `useKeptReadingScroll`, the line `let restoring = place.scrollTops.get(scope) ?? 0;` was changed to `let restoring = 0;`. The saved scroll offset is then never restored when the pane remounts. Fixtures and assertions were left unchanged. The G6 path ("without cycling the Done tabs first") was not chosen. The plan's G6 disposition argues the cycle ends on the same tab without reselecting the file, so a fault confined to the no-cycle path is less plausible than a restore fault.

Scratch checkout: detached `git worktree add` at /Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/359d7314/tmp/ic-scratch, with its own `npm ci` (Node v24.21.0, matches .node-version). Pre-probe `git status --porcelain` was empty. Removed afterwards with `git worktree remove --force`.

Command (run in scratch): PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES npx playwright test --config dashboard/frontend.playwright.config.ts --workers=1 --reporter=list dashboard/frontend-tests/intent/intent-done-project-refresh.spec.ts
Load during runs: 1-minute load average about 3.9-4.7.

Results:
- Baseline: 1 passed (test 5.1s, run 8.2s).
- Faulted: 1 failed at intent-done-project-refresh.spec.ts:143, `await expect.poll(() => intentReadingScroll(intent)).toBe(offset);`, with Expected: 968, Received: 0 (5s poll timeout). Earlier assertions passed (selection aria-pressed, Purpose tab aria-selected, diff aria-busy), so the run reached the return path.
- Independent witness: a scratch-only copy of the case, with line 143 replaced by a 1s wait, a log of the saved offset and the pane's scrollTop after return, and an early end. Under the fault it logged "saved offset 968 after return 0". With the fault reverted it logged "saved offset 968 after return 968". This shows the reading place goes wrong on the intended project-refresh return path. It also shows the halfway scroll reaches a real nonzero offset.
- Restore: the fault was reverted with `git checkout -- dashboard/src/pageIntentReading.tsx` (a shell trap was also armed) and the witness spec was deleted. `git status --porcelain` was then empty (only the ignored test-results/ remained), matching the pre-probe state. Rerunning the same command: 1 passed (test 4.4s, run 5.1s).

Verdict: Caught. The maintained assertion `expect.poll(() => intentReadingScroll(intent)).toBe(offset)` at dashboard/frontend-tests/intent/intent-done-project-refresh.spec.ts:143 failed on independently observed wrong behavior: scroll place 0 instead of 968. The observed path was: project refresh after cycling all Done tabs, Project Intent visit with Show latest revision, then Back to story.

Next proof action: none required for the reading-place rule on this path, because the merged survivor catches a lost-restore fault there. Optionally, the caller may record this third scratch break with the two existing ones in the slice 6 Result.

Prior disposition: the evidence matches and supports slice 6's merge claim and G6's "no user cost" disposition for the reading place on the cycled path. It does not test the uncycled path that G6 names. No new repair decision arises from this probe.

Costs:
- Test runtime (measured, Playwright reporter wall time per run): baseline 8.2s; the faulted maintained run failed after about 8.4s of test time; faulted witness 5.8s; restored witness 5.4s; restored maintained 5.1s. Test runs total about 33s, excluding `npm ci`, which was not timed separately.
- Human effort: unavailable. No human took part in this probe and there is no separate measure.
